verses.verse:
मुखतो वायु निर्धातः फूत्कार इति कथ्यते।
प्राकृतो वैकृतश्चैव कृत्रिमस्तु तृतीयकः।६५।
verses.text: The issuing of air from the mouth is called phūtkāra (blowing). It is prākṛta (natural) and vaikṛta (cultivated), and the third is kṛtrima (artificial).

commentary.text: That is, the directed issue, that is, the flow, of air from the mouth is called phūtkāra, that is, phūṅk (blowing). It has three kinds: prākṛta (natural), vaikṛta (cultivated) and kṛtrima (artificial). The Tripurā bānsurī is played with natural blowing, the āḍī (transverse) bānsurī with cultivated blowing, and the bānsurī with a jibbhī (fipple) with artificial blowing. For natural blowing no mukharandhra (mouth-hole) of any kind has to be made in the bānsurī; the sound is made by the player's skill alone. For cultivated blowing a mouth-hole and a cork have to be provided, and the player makes [the breath] fit for sound with some effort. For artificial blowing the bānsurī maker has to make all the effort, and the player gets the sound out easily. Man follows the middle path, so for him cultivated blowing is the best.

subsection.title: Practice of the Tongue and of the Fingers

terms.en: blowing — air directed from the mouth into the bānsurī
